text:
emma: Quick thread after today's all-hands Q&A  putting travel/hybrid/offsite policy clarifications here so folks can find them later. Short answers first, details below.

ryan: Thanks! Two things: 1) If I book personal upgrades (e.g., upgrade to comfort) and want reimbursement later, is that allowed? 2) What's the policy for short-term "workation" (working from a different US city for <2 weeks)?

emma: 1) Personal-paid upgrades are not reimbursable unless pre-approved by your manager due to schedule/medical reasons. If manager pre-approves, attach approval to the expense. 2) Workations under 14 days: file a Remote Location Request and notify people-ops; usually approved for domestic travel. Cross-border workations need finance/legal sign-off.

people-ops-bot: New: Workation & Travel FAQ uploaded -> https://intranet.redwood/policies/workation_faq (edited)

nate: Is there a separate process for bringing a +1 to an offsite? Like partner/child on multi-day retreat?

emma: Partners/guests are allowed ONLY for social/regional meetups where stated. For company retreats or customer-facing events, guests are not permitted unless explicitly approved. If approved, guests are self-pay unless manager signs off. Policy examples are in the doc.

lena: Question: coworking day passes vs coworking stipend  can I use the stipend to cover a 3-day coworking pass while traveling?

emma: The monthly coworking stipend ($150) is for recurring use and can't be retro-applied per trip. For short trips, submit day-pass receipts under "Travel - Other" (limit $30/day) and we'll reimburse with receipts. If you routinely need coworking while traveling, opt into the stipend.

product-ops: Clarify conference attendance: if I bring a client or partner as a guest to a paid conference, is that allowed and who pays?

emma: Conference guest policy: client invites must be pre-cleared by your manager and legal (conflict-of-interest). Tickets for non-employees are not company-paid unless it's a sponsored/partner event with explicit budget.

ryan: Any updates on hoteling desks at HQ? I keep seeing double-book conflicts when teams schedule rooms + desks.

emma: Hoteling improvements roll out next sprint: meeting rooms will have reserved buffer slots tied to the meeting invite. For now, priority order is meeting organizer > recurring desk owner > one-off hoteling. If you see a conflict, open a ticket in #desk-ops and ops will reconcile.

people-ops-bot: Desk reservation guidelines: https://intranet.redwood/office/desks (pinned)

ceo: One leadership note: for Dedicated customer visits to our data centers or partner sites, security clearance & visitor badges must be requested at least 72 hours prior. No last-minute walk-ins.

nate: Are we covering pet-friendly accommodations if someone needs to bring a service animal?

emma: Service animals are allowed and the company will cover reasonable fees. For non-service pets, not covered unless pre-approved as a disability accommodation (work with HR).

lena: If managers want to run a small voluntary team offsite (<=3 days), is there a budget cap per person?

emma: Small team offsites: default cap $350/person/day (covers lodging, meals, local transport) unless you submit a larger budget & leadership approval. Use the "Offsite Budget Request" form.

ryan: Any extra care around tax implications for frequent travel across states?

emma: Short domestic trips typically do not change payroll state, but frequent relocations or >30 days in a state may. Finance runs reviews for anything >30 days — submit early. Cross-border is PCP with legal.

product-ops: Who to contact for childcare stipend pre-approval?

emma: Managers submit a request via people-ops; childcare approvals are case-by-case for mandatory company travel. Receipts and manager note required.

ryan: thanks, super helpful. I'll pass to my manager for any pre-approvals.

emma: I'll consolidate this into a short FAQ and post a one-pager with quick flows (workation, guest rules, reimbursements) by Friday. Volunteers to review?
